summary: CDAS proposes a JSD distribution-matching objective with distributed interchange interventions as a weaker, more ‘faithful’ alternative to Lang./PO steering. The framing is coherent and the safety case studies (refusal override, CoT backdoor) are relevant, but the main AXBENCH results are mixed and often behind RePS, while the claimed tuning-free / on-distribution factor story is undermined by large unit-vs-tuned gaps. The paper is close to the ICLR borderline but needs stronger isolation of design choices, broader evidence for claimed complementarities, and tighter claim–evidence alignment before acceptance.
strengths: Clear conceptual framing that ties intervention steering to causal-feature localization ideas (DII/DAS) rather than treating steering as PEFT-lite.
Training objective is well motivated: full-vocabulary JSD matching to the model’s own counterfactual distribution is a plausible weaker alternative to Lang./PO.
Empirical scope is non-trivial: AXBENCH plus multi-scale refusal (up to 70B) and a challenging backdoor suppression setting, with utility/KL checks that support a faithfulness narrative.
Calibration is better than many steering papers: the authors explicitly report losses to RePS/Lang., layer sensitivity, and limitations (data requirements, factor tuning, rank-1 only).

key_concerns.issue: Primary AXBENCH evidence does not establish a clear advance: RePS remains the strongest overall, CDAS wins mainly at Gemma-2-9B L20 with tuned factors, and unit-factor CDAS is weak—undercutting the claim that DII’s implicit factor sampling yields faithful, tuning-light control.
key_concerns.suggested_fix: Either strengthen unit-factor / principled-factor protocols until competitive, or reframe CDAS as a utility-preserving / large-model niche method and add decisive settings where that niche is the evaluation target rather than general-purpose AXBENCH leadership.

key_concerns.issue: Insufficient ablations isolate what drives gains: JSD vs KL/other f-divergences, distribution matching vs DII, one-to-many source-token choice, and clamping-at-inference vs training-time DII are not systematically dissected beyond the partially informative DAS (Lang.+DII) baseline.
key_concerns.suggested_fix: Add a factorial ablation table (objective × intervention protocol × factor schedule) on a fixed data/model setup, plus sensitivity to source-token position beyond a single grid-search optimum.

key_concerns.issue: Breadth is limited relative to generality claims about bi-directional faithful steering and scale benefits: main benchmark is Gemma-only; case-study wins are uneven (fails refusal suppression on Phi-3.5-mini); layer selection sometimes optimized for DIM; BiPO omitted from case studies.
key_concerns.suggested_fix: Evaluate at least one non-Gemma family on AXBENCH-style concepts, report refusal/backdoor with pre-registered layers or method-agnostic layer sweeps, and include PO baselines consistently with the same factor budgets.

key_concerns.issue: Statistical reporting is incomplete for an empirical steering paper: AXBENCH and refusal tables largely lack seed-level variance/significance; judge-based metrics rely on gpt-4o-mini that also helps construct training data, risking correlated evaluation bias.
key_concerns.suggested_fix: Report multi-seed means±SE for all optimized methods, pairwise significance where margins are small, and at least one held-out human or alternate-judge check on concept/refusal scores.

key_concerns.issue: Naming and positioning of the ‘DAS’ baseline (Lang. objective under DII) collide with standard DAS/causal localization terminology and may confuse contribution delineation.
key_concerns.suggested_fix: Rename the Lang.+DII control (e.g., Lang-DII) and sharpen related-work contrast against causal localization vs steering goals already noted in the remark.

questions_for_authors: Given large unit-vs-tuned gaps on AXBENCH, what evidence remains that DII-sampled factors are meaningfully more on-distribution than RePS’s factor sampling at matched inference budgets?
Does replacing JSD with token-level CE/KL to the counterfactual distribution recover or destroy CDAS’s utility/KL advantages in the refusal and backdoor settings?
How sensitive are fair AXBENCH scores to the gpt-4o-mini augmentation templates and to the choice of the single <model> source token?
For refusal experiments, what happens if layer and factor selection are optimized independently per method rather than via DIM’s suppression-maximizing layer?
calibration_check: Claims are partially well scoped in the conclusion (complementary, not always better; prefers larger models / utility preservation), but the title and early framing of faithful bi-directional steering still overreach relative to mixed AXBENCH results and dependence on tuned factors.

significance.justification: Steering reliability and safety override are timely ICLR topics, and a utility-preserving alternative would be cited, but impact is capped by inconsistent wins against strong existing steering methods.

novelty.justification: Combining DII with full-vocabulary JSD matching for steering is a genuine and useful twist on DAS/PO/Lang., yet it is still an incremental recombination of known localization and distillation ingredients rather than a new paradigm.

rigor.justification: Method derivation is coherent and the DAS vs CDAS contrast helps attribute the objective, but layer/factor protocols and evaluation construction introduce confounds that weaken causal support for the faithfulness story.

statistical_soundness.justification: Some multi-split AXBENCH fair scores and three-seed backdoor ASR with SE exist, but most headline tables lack seed variance or significance tests and rely on single-judge automated scores.

calibration_honesty.justification: The paper openly reports underperformance vs RePS/Lang., layer fragility, and a solid limitations section, though the ‘faithful/tuning-light’ rhetoric is ahead of the unit-factor evidence.

clarity.justification: Organization and problem setup are clear for an expert audience; equations and protocols are mostly precise despite dense prose and occasional naming confusion around DAS.

structure_compliance.justification: Standard ICLR flow (intro, related work, method, benchmark, case studies, conclusion/limitations) is complete and appropriately scoped for a conference paper.

reproducibility.justification: Data construction, DII protocol, objectives, factor schedules, models/layers, and evaluation metrics are described in enough detail to reimplement if assets were available; remaining gaps are mainly exact grids and judge prompts.

related_work.justification: Steering, DAS/localization, distillation/JSD, and safety-mechanism lines are fairly positioned, but comparison depth to concurrent optimized steering variants is uneven outside AXBENCH.

figure_quality.justification: Captions describe informative comparative tables and layer-wise ASR curves with uncertainty that directly support the core empirical claims rather than decorate them.

breadth_generality.justification: Evidence spans concepts and two safety tasks, but Gemma-only AXBENCH, rank-1 only, omitted case-study PO baselines, and uneven small-model results under-support the generality implied by the framing.

overall_recommendation.justification: Promising and honestly framed, but mixed primary results plus missing ablations/breadth keep it at borderline reject until the complementary-advantage story is experimentally decisive.
